## BL-214 — Drill-through: one progressive-disclosure idiom

**Status: settled 2026-07-30.** Authority for the concept is `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` § Drill-through
(new section, sibling to § Container vocabulary). This item lands the vocabulary, the shared
control, and the wiring of the six surfaces named below.

### The reframe: three axes, not four idioms

The four idioms were never four answers to one question. They were **three different questions**
wearing one costume. Naming the three is most of the fix:

| Axis | Question | Gesture | Control | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Depth** (this item) | *How much of this subject do I want?* | Expand **in place** | `ui::detail_stepper` — three-segment stepper | `ui_state::detail[]` |
| **Subject** (BL-196, built) | *What am I looking at?* | Click the element | Breadcrumb + `<` back | `ui_state::card_stack` |
| **Host** (SELECTION.md, built) | *Where does this properly live?* | `[>]` go-to | `ui::focus_on_entity` | `active_body` / `show_*` |

BL-196 is therefore **not folded in and not a competitor** — it is the sibling axis, and its
`card_stack`, breadcrumb and acyclicity rules are untouched. The Corporation dashboard's roll-ups
"clicking through into the relevant per-system ledger" are a **host** change, not depth, and are
correct as designed. Only the History explainer, the tile accordion's withheld derivation, and the
wizard's prose are depth.

### The closed set

```
GLANCE  — a figure and its direction. Labels, numbers, verdict words, glyphs. No sentences.
READ    — the compact composed view. + charts (with full legends: swatch · label · value)
          and interactive sub-controls (pagers, scrubbers, action grids).
STUDY   — the full derivation. + wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes,
          derivation breadcrumbs, secondary/wide table columns.
```

**Content class table** — the only thing an implementer needs to decide where a widget belongs:

| Content class | Glance | Read | Study |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Load-bearing figures, labels, verdict words, glyphs | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Charts and their legends (swatch · label · **value**) | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| Interactive sub-controls (pagers, scrubbers, action grids) | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| Wrapped prose (explainers, consequences, why-lines) | — | — | ✓ |
| Threshold **captions**, annotated axes, derivation breadcrumbs | — | — | ✓ |
| Secondary / wide table columns beyond identity + key numerics | — | — | ✓ |

Note the threshold **line** is a chart element (Read); only its **caption** is Study. Legend
**values** stay at Read: a legend value is a load-bearing figure and demoting it would be
truncation by another name.

### Two invariants

1. **Levels are strictly additive.** A higher level never removes a load-bearing figure a lower
   level showed. The whole model is one monotone predicate —
   `shows(s, ui, want) == (detail_level_of(s, ui) >= want)` — and every content site is a single
   `if (shows(...))` with **no `else`**, no per-level layout variant, and no re-layout on change.
   This is what makes "expand, don't replace" fall out of the implementation instead of out of
   discipline.
2. **Every guaranteed-fit container is Glance-only.** LAYOUT.md containers **2** (on-canvas lens
   legend), **4** (header/balance strip), **5** (time panel), **7** (minimap lens bar) and
   **9-numeric** (table cells) offer no depth control at all. Levels only ever grow inside a
   **wrap** container (1, 3, 6, 9-description). Consequence: **drill-through adds no tenth
   container.** The nine say *how text fits*; the three say *how much text there is*. No level
   change can create a new overflow site.

### The authored policy table

`def` is **authored, never computed** — a default derived from the live region would twitch on
resize. The authoring criterion is: *the level at which the surface answers its own question in
one screenful at **1280×720***. `lo` follows a derived rule: a **fixed-rect** container's `lo` is
the level its rect was authored for; a **stretch/scroll** container's `lo` may be `glance`.

| `detail_surface` | lo | hi | **def** | What each level is, here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selection_band` | read | study | **read** | Fixed 340 px rect (`selection_band_height`) authored for Read — Glance would leave it half-empty. Read = today's content (hex neighbourhood + accordion + action grid, or the action\|facts split). Study adds the accordion's threshold captions and the tile derivation breadcrumb. |
| `selection_drill` | read | study | **read** | Same fixed rect. Read = the BL-196 time series + scrubber. Study adds the annotated axis and the "Recording began here…" provenance line. |
| `history_story` | glance | study | **read** | Glance = the archetype + span line only. Read = the dated `ev.event` lines. Study = + each line's indented `ev.consequence` paragraph. Read is the view's question, so Read is the default. |
| `history_chain` | glance | study | **glance** | Glance = one verdict line per stage in the round (`Lost here: Cinder` / `all passed`), which fits the 324 px column in one screenful. Read = + each stage's charts. Study = + `stage_explainer()` prose and threshold captions. Four stages of charts do **not** fit one screenful — this is the rule producing the answer, not an assertion. |
| `history_tiles` | read | study | **read** | Read = X / Y / composition / landform / hazard / habitability. Study = + the 23 per-resource columns (today's horizontal-scroll offender). |
| `generation_wizard` | read | study | **study** | **The one named exception** to the default criterion (see below). Read strips the explainers for a replaying player. |

**The wizard exception, stated explicitly rather than by omission.** `generation_wizard` does not
fit Study in one screenful and gets Study anyway, because for this surface the depth *is* the
feature (BL-167: "the first thing a player sees"). It participates rather than being exempt for
three reasons: it becomes the **teacher** of the idiom (the gesture is learned before the first
ledger opens); a Read rung is a real want an exemption would have destroyed (a replaying player
wants the charts without the chemistry); and "first contact" is an argument about first contact,
which the **reset-to-Study-on-entry** rule honours exactly.

### Memory

The chosen level is **remembered per surface, for the session** (`ui_state::detail`), and is
**not serialised** — the same policy as `economy_view` / `history_view`. A **subject** change
(selecting a different tile, switching the History body combo) does **not** reset it; that is the
point of remembering. A **new campaign** resets it via `ui::reset_detail_levels(ui_state&)`, which
also runs on entering the generation screen from the main menu so the wizard always opens at Study.
A BL-196 drilled frame opens at its parent's level, **clamped** to `selection_drill`'s own range.

### The control

`ui::detail_stepper(detail_surface, ui_state&)` — a composite control, **not** a `ui::icons` glyph
(the icons contract is `(dl, centre, r, colour)`; a lit-segment count does not fit it, and no
ICONS.md entry is owed).

- **Placement, identical on every surface:** the surface's title row, right-aligned, immediately
  **left** of the `[>]` go-to / `[x]` close cluster.
- **Shape:** one `ImGui::InvisibleButton("##depth", {h * 2.2f, h})` with `h = GetFrameHeight()`,
  hit-split into three equal columns. Draws three baseline-aligned rounded bars of ascending
  height (`0.35h / 0.60h / 0.85h`) — the shape says *amount*. Segments at index ≤ current lit with
  `palette::selection`; higher segments at ~35 % alpha; segments outside `[lo, hi]` at ~15 % alpha
  and not clickable.
- **Draws nothing at all** when `lo == hi` (a single-level surface has no control).
- Hover tooltip: `Detail: Read  (Glance / Read / Study)`.
- **Not a toggle.** Exempt as a cross-cutting selector — the level set has **no null member**, so
  there is nothing to undo *to*, exactly as re-picking a resource in a lens combo is a no-op. This
  is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the standing rule's existing exemption clause;
  `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` is **not** edited. Re-clicking the active segment is a no-op
  — deliberately **not** "revert to default", which would be the locally-clever/opaque option and
  would make this the one control in the app whose re-click means *revert* while adjacent
  `nav_button` strips' re-click means *close*.
- **No keyboard binding, and it does not join the Esc ladder** (`app.cpp`, order today:
  `confirm_exit_pending` → `show_system_menu` → pop `card_stack` → hide selection → open system
  menu). Depth is not a dismissal; `card_stack` (subject) already owns that unwind, and a second
  one would re-merge the axes at the keyboard.

### Code shape

**New pair `src/ui/detail_level.{hpp,cpp}`.** No `CMakeLists.txt` edit is needed —
`file(GLOB_RECURSE GAME_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "src/*.cpp")` (CMakeLists.txt:89) picks it up.
Enums sit at **global** scope alongside `canvas_level` / `overlay_mode` (the file's existing
convention); functions sit in `namespace ui`. `struct ui_state;` is forward-declared so
`ui_state.hpp` may include this header without a cycle.

```cpp
// src/ui/detail_level.hpp
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

struct ui_state; // fwd — the widget takes it by reference only

/// The closed set of disclosure levels (BL-214). Ordered: higher = strictly more
/// content. Levels are ADDITIVE — a higher level never removes a load-bearing
/// figure a lower one showed. See docs/ui/LAYOUT.md § Drill-through.
enum class detail_level : std::uint8_t
{
    glance = 0, ///< Figures, labels, verdict words, glyphs. No sentences.
    read   = 1, ///< + charts (with full legends) and interactive sub-controls.
    study  = 2, ///< + wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes, wide columns.
};

/// Every site that owns a depth control. Indexes ui_state::detail.
/// Adding a surface = an enumerator here, a row in detail_policy_of, and one
/// `shows()` branch per gated content class. Nothing else.
enum class detail_surface : std::uint8_t
{
    selection_band = 0, ///< Selection band root content (selection_panel.cpp).
    selection_drill,    ///< A BL-196 drilled frame in the band (selection_card.cpp).
    history_story,      ///< History ledger, Story view (tile_inspector.cpp).
    history_chain,      ///< History ledger, Chain view.
    history_tiles,      ///< History ledger, Tiles view.
    generation_wizard,  ///< The New World wizard (app.cpp draw_generation_screen).
    count
};
inline constexpr std::size_t detail_surface_count =
    static_cast<std::size_t>(detail_surface::count);

/// What one surface declares: the inclusive level range it can render, and where
/// it opens. Authored, never computed at runtime — a default derived from the live
/// region would twitch on resize. lo <= def <= hi always.
struct detail_policy { detail_level lo, hi, def; };

namespace ui {
const detail_policy& detail_policy_of(detail_surface s);
void         reset_detail_levels(ui_state& ui);                       ///< All surfaces -> their def.
detail_level detail_level_of(detail_surface s, const ui_state& ui);   ///< Clamped to the policy.
bool         shows(detail_surface s, const ui_state& ui, detail_level want); ///< THE predicate.
bool         detail_stepper(detail_surface s, ui_state& ui);          ///< true on frames the level changed.
} // namespace ui
```

**State** — one line in `ui_state` (`src/ui/ui_state.hpp`), beside the `economy_view` /
`history_view` block it shares a policy with:

```cpp
    /// Per-surface disclosure level (BL-214), one entry per detail_surface, values
    /// are detail_level. VIEW state: remembered for the session so a player who asks
    /// for depth keeps it across reopens and across subject changes; NOT serialised
    /// (same policy as economy_view / history_view). Seeded by ui::reset_detail_levels.
    std::array<std::uint8_t, detail_surface_count> detail{};
```

**The wiring is uniformly one branch per site.** Worked example, `generation_charts.cpp`:

```cpp
    const bool study = (lvl >= detail_level::study);
    if (study) dim_para(stage_explainer(s));
    // `Lost here: Cinder` is a label + list — a GLANCE-class verdict, always drawn.
    if (lvl >= detail_level::read) { /* the chart_row() calls */ }
    // Caption gated, LINE not: auto cap = [&](const char* c){ return study ? c : nullptr; };
    charts::threshold_line(dl, mn, mx, 1.0512f, c, col_gate, cap("runaway greenhouse"));
```

`charts::threshold_line` gains a two-line guard: a null/empty `caption` draws the line and skips
the caption. That single change removes, at the default level, the `"ay greenhouse"` clip
committed in `scripts/verify/golden/history_chain_round0.png` today.

**Header factoring (foundation).** The three structurally-identical Selection headers —
generic (`selection_panel.cpp` ~:1186-1219), tile (~:590-604), drill (`selection_card.cpp` :36-62)
— become one `ui::draw_selection_header(...)`, so the stepper is added once rather than in three
places kept in sync. This is the recon's own recommendation and is a prerequisite, not a
nice-to-have: adding the stepper to three copies is how the fourth idiom gets born.

### Relationship to BL-215 (shared file scope — plan the collision)

The seam, stated flatly so neither item does the other's work:

> **BL-214 decides WHETHER a string is drawn. BL-215 decides HOW a string that is drawn fits its
> container.** A withheld paragraph is not a BL-215 fix; a clipped chart title is not a BL-214 fix.

**BL-214 lands first**, so BL-215's render-precision audit measures the reduced set. The two share
`docs/ui/LAYOUT.md`, `src/ui/charts.cpp`, `src/ui/generation_charts.cpp`,
`src/ui/selection_panel.cpp` and `src/ui/tile_inspector.cpp` — run them sequentially in one batch,
not as concurrent worktree agents.

### Extension recipe (so surface #7 does not invent idiom #5)

Adding a surface to the ladder is exactly three edits: an enumerator in `detail_surface`; a row in
`detail_policy_of` (with `lo` from the fixed-rect/stretch rule and `def` from the one-screenful-at-
1280×720 criterion); and one `if (shows(...))` per gated content class. `ui::detail_stepper` is
called once on the surface's title row. Nothing else — no new control, no new state, no new doc
section. The Corporation dashboard's four roll-ups (MENU.md slot 1, not yet built) are the first
expected caller; the enumerator is deliberately **not** added ahead of the wiring.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben was unavailable; these are authoritative and auditable.

1. **Three levels — Glance / Read / Study — as a closed set**, declared per surface as an inclusive
   range `[lo, hi]` plus a `def`, not as three mandatory rungs. Two rungs is the collapse that
   produced the problem; four-plus is a spectrum, not a vocabulary.
2. **The uniform gesture is one shared stepper with expand-in-place as the only response** — and
   the answer *names the other two gestures* (subject / host) so they stop competing. BL-196 is
   the sibling axis, untouched, not folded in.
3. **Defaults are authored per surface**, criterion = *answers its own question in one screenful at
   1280×720*; `lo` = the fixed rect's authored level, or `glance` where the container scrolls.
   Yields Read / Read / Read / **Glance** / Read / **Study**. **Rejected: Glance everywhere** — a
   fixed-rect container cannot shrink, so a Glance Selection band spends 340 px on emptiness.
4. **The level is remembered per surface, session-only, not serialised**; a subject change does not
   reset it, a new campaign does.
5. **The wizard participates**, with the sole named exception to the default criterion
   (`def = study`) and a reset-to-Study on entering the generation screen. **Rejected: exempting
   it** — exemption by omission is what created this item, and participation makes the wizard the
   idiom's teacher.
6. **Prose is a Study-only content class — withheld, never truncated.** Legend *values* stay at
   Read (a load-bearing figure); threshold *captions* move to Study (an annotation).
7. **Levels are strictly additive**, expressed as the single monotone `shows()` predicate with no
   `else` branch anywhere.
8. **Every guaranteed-fit container is Glance-only**, so drill-through adds no tenth container and
   can never create a new overflow site.
9. **The stepper is exempt from the toggle rule** as a cross-cutting selector (no null member in
   the set); re-click is a no-op, **not** revert-to-default. No `io-standing-rules.md` edit; the
   exemption is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the rule's existing clause.
10. **No keyboard binding and no place on the Esc ladder** — `card_stack` already owns that unwind
    and depth must not double-book it.
11. **BL-214 lands before BL-215**, with the whether/how seam stated; the two run sequentially,
    not as concurrent worktree agents.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben delegated these calls for the ultracode session and was unavailable; each is recorded here so it can be reviewed or overturned.

**Q. 1. How many disclosure levels, what are they called, and must every surface place itself on the ladder?**

- **Decision:** THREE levels — GLANCE / READ / STUDY — declared as a closed set in `enum class detail_level` (src/ui/detail_level.hpp). Every *dense* surface declares itself on the ladder, but as an inclusive RANGE `[lo, hi]` plus a `def`, not as all three rungs. A surface whose `lo == hi` is single-level, draws no depth control, and is thereby explicitly on the ladder rather than silently outside it. Six surfaces are enumerated in the first landing: selection_band, selection_drill, history_story, history_chain, history_tiles, generation_wizard.
- **Why:** Two rungs is the collapse that produced the problem — 'compact vs full' is exactly what each of the four surfaces already invented separately; the useful middle rung ('the compact composed view') is where nearly every ledger actually sits today, so a two-value enum would force History's Chain and the Selection band to share a value they do not share. Four-plus is a spectrum, not a vocabulary, and LAYOUT.md's nine-container precedent is that the value comes from the set being closed and small. Three also maps 1:1 onto the three content classes the codebase already has: a figure, a chart, a paragraph. Declaring a RANGE rather than three rungs is what lets a Glance-only container (the header strip, the hover card) participate honestly instead of being an unstated exception — the same failure mode this item exists to kill.

**Q. 2. What is the uniform gesture — expand-in-place, child card (BL-196), or go-to? And must it mean the same thing everywhere?**

- **Decision:** The gesture is ONE shared control — `ui::detail_stepper`, a three-segment stepper — placed in a fixed position on every multi-level surface's title row (right-aligned, immediately LEFT of the `[>]` go-to / `[x]` close cluster), and EXPAND-IN-PLACE is the only permitted rendering response. Crucially, the answer also names what the other two gestures are, so they stop competing: they are not depth at all. Three orthogonal axes, three controls, never conflated — DEPTH (how much of this subject: the stepper, expand in place, BL-214); SUBJECT (what am I looking at: click the element, breadcrumb, child frame, BL-196's `ui.card_stack`); HOST (where does this live: `[>]`, `ui::focus_on_entity`, SELECTION.md's existing 'reference one hop away'). Yes, it means the same thing everywhere — that is the whole item.
- **Why:** The four idioms were never four answers to 'how do I show more'; they were three different QUESTIONS wearing one costume. The Corporation roll-up 'clicking through into a per-system ledger' is a host change. BL-196's child card is a subject change. Only the History explainer and the tile accordion's withheld derivation are depth. Once the axes are separated, BL-196 needs no folding-in and no competing — it is the sibling axis, and its breadcrumb (which is a SUBJECT-path indicator) is left exactly as built. A stepper rather than a cycling button because the level is state whose current value must be visible; a cycling button hides where you are, and an absolute selector never needs pressing twice. Expand-in-place is mandated because the 2026-07-23 UX note's finding was precisely that a mode-switch reads as 'the thing I was reading vanished', and because levels are strictly additive (Decision 6) the expansion is implementable top-down without moving anything already on screen.

**Q. 3. What is the default level per surface, and is it remembered?**

- **Decision:** The default is AUTHORED per surface in one table (`ui::detail_policy_of`), never computed at runtime. The authoring criterion: the default is the level at which the surface answers its own question in ONE SCREENFUL at 1280x720. That yields — selection_band READ, selection_drill READ, history_story READ, history_chain GLANCE, history_tiles READ, generation_wizard STUDY. A second derived rule fixes `lo`: a FIXED-RECT container's `lo` is the level its rect was authored for (so the 340px Selection band's `lo` is READ, not GLANCE); a stretch/scroll container's `lo` may be GLANCE. And YES, the player's chosen level IS remembered — per surface, for the session, in `ui_state::detail`, NOT serialised (same policy as `economy_view` / `history_view`). A subject change (selecting a different tile, switching body) does NOT reset it; a new campaign does, via `ui::reset_detail_levels`.
- **Why:** GLANCE-everywhere is the tempting answer and it is wrong for exactly one structural reason: a fixed-rect container cannot shrink. A GLANCE Selection band still occupies 340 fixed px (`selection_band_height`), so the level below the rect's authored level buys nothing and spends the band on dead space — density in a fixed rect beats emptiness. Where the container DOES stretch and scroll, GLANCE is honest and earns its keep: History's Chain at 324px column width fits four stage-verdict lines in one screenful and cannot fit four stages of charts, so its default drops to GLANCE and the item's instinct is vindicated by the rule rather than by assertion. Authored-not-computed because a default derived from the live region would twitch on resize, which is worse than any wrong constant. Remembered because a player who asks for depth is in a reading mood and will ask again in thirty seconds; making them re-ask each reopen is precisely the friction that makes depth feel expensive, which is the behaviour this item is trying to remove. Session-only because it is view state and the save format must not grow for it.

**Q. 4. Does the wizard participate?**

- **Decision:** YES — explicitly, and it is the one NAMED EXCEPTION to the default-authoring criterion. `generation_wizard` declares `lo = read, hi = study, def = study`. It does not fit STUDY in one screenful at 1280x720 and gets STUDY anyway, because for this surface the depth IS the feature. It is reset to STUDY on entering the generation screen from the main menu, so a fresh campaign always opens at full depth.
- **Why:** Exempting it by omission is what created this item, so it must participate or be named — and participating is strictly the stronger option for three concrete reasons. (a) It becomes the TEACHER of the idiom: the wizard is the first thing a player sees (BL-167), so meeting the stepper there means the gesture is already learned before the first ledger opens — the idiom's rollout is free. (b) A READ rung is a real want the exemption would have destroyed: a replaying player who has read ten stages of chemistry once wants the charts without the prose, and today has no way to ask. (c) 'First contact' is an argument about first contact specifically, which the reset-to-STUDY-on-entry rule honours exactly; it is not an argument for being outside the vocabulary. The exception is to the DEFAULT rule only, it is one row in the table, and it is written down rather than implied.

**Q. 5. Text density — how do the two-paragraph stage explainers behave, and how does this couple to BL-215?**

- **Decision:** Wrapped prose is a STUDY-ONLY content class. A paragraph is WITHHELD below STUDY — never truncated, never summarised, never demoted to a tooltip. Concretely: GLANCE renders figures, labels, verdict words and glyphs (no sentences); READ adds charts with their full legends (swatch, label AND value) and interactive sub-controls; STUDY adds wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes, derivation breadcrumbs, and secondary/wide table columns. `stage_explainer()` renders at STUDY only. `charts::threshold_line`'s CAPTION is STUDY-only (the LINE itself is a chart element and stays at READ). The seam with BL-215 is stated flatly: **BL-214 decides WHETHER a string is drawn; BL-215 decides HOW a string that is drawn fits its container.** BL-214 lands FIRST, so BL-215's audit measures the reduced set and does not spend effort fitting strings this item withholds.
- **Why:** Truncating a paragraph is the LAYOUT.md ban being broken in a new place, and 'a shorter explainer' is content-cutting, which is the item's stated non-goal. Withholding is neither: the paragraph is intact and one click away. Legend VALUES are deliberately kept at READ rather than pushed to STUDY, because a legend value is a load-bearing figure and moving it up a rung would be truncation by another name — which is why the load-bearing invariant (Decision 6) exists. The BL-215 coupling is real and pays immediately: gating the threshold caption at STUDY removes, at the default level, the exact `"ay greenhouse"` clip that is committed in `scripts/verify/golden/history_chain_round0.png` today. Ordering BL-214 first avoids fixing that clip twice.

**Q. 6. What keeps this from being a content cut in disguise, and what is the invariant an implementer must not break?**

- **Decision:** LEVELS ARE STRICTLY ADDITIVE. A higher level never removes a load-bearing figure a lower level showed. Formally the whole model is one predicate: `shows(surface, ui, want) == (detail_level_of(surface, ui) >= want)`, and every content site is a single `if (shows(...))` branch — there is no `else`, no per-level layout variant, and no re-layout on level change. Second invariant, which is what makes the model safe against BL-215: EVERY GUARANTEED-FIT CONTAINER IS GLANCE-ONLY. LAYOUT.md containers 2 (lens legend), 4 (header strip), 5 (time panel), 7 (minimap lens bar) and 9-numeric (table cells) offer no depth control at all; levels only ever grow inside a WRAP container. Drill-through therefore adds NO tenth container — it is an orthogonal axis over the existing nine: the nine say how text fits, the three say how much text there is.
- **Why:** 'Expand, don't replace' (the 2026-07-23 UX note) is unenforceable as advice and trivial as an invariant — strict additivity makes it fall out of the implementation rather than out of discipline, since content drawn top-down and gated by a monotone predicate cannot move what is already on screen. The guaranteed-fit/Glance-only alignment is not a coincidence to be admired: it is the safety property. A container that measures text to size itself can never be handed a paragraph, so no level change can ever create a new overflow site — which is the one way this item could otherwise have made BL-215 worse instead of better.

**Q. 7. Does the depth stepper obey the universal toggle rule (re-clicking an active control undoes it)?**

- **Decision:** NO — it is EXEMPT, as a cross-cutting selector. Clicking the already-active segment is a no-op. This is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the standing rule's existing exemption clause; `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` is NOT edited. The stepper also takes no keyboard binding and does NOT join the Esc ladder in `app.cpp` (order today: confirm_exit -> system menu -> pop `card_stack` -> hide selection -> open system menu) — a level is not a dismissal and must not consume an unwind.
- **Why:** The standing rule exempts cross-cutting selectors 'which switch a target rather than express an active state', and the discriminating property is that a selector's set has NO NULL MEMBER — a resource combo has no null resource, and a surface always renders at SOME level. There is nothing for a toggle to undo TO. The clever reading ('re-click returns to the surface's default') is exactly the locally-clever/opaque solution the tone guidance rejects: it is invisible, unguessable, and it would make the one control in the app whose re-click means 'revert' sit next to nav_button strips whose re-click means 'close'. Staying off the Esc ladder matters because `card_stack` (SUBJECT) already owns an unwind there; giving DEPTH a second unwind would make Esc's meaning depend on invisible state, re-merging the two axes at the keyboard that Decision 2 just separated in the UI.
BL-214.resolution: Complete. Landed the BINARY fold model (Ben s 2026-07-31 supersession), not the three-level stepper: folded = a verdict line + a single chevron, expanded = a true full-screen overlay. State is one (surface, key) target rather than a per-surface remembered level - that falls out of expanded being an overlay, so only one thing can be expanded at a time. Six surfaces wired: the Selection band metric card, History Story/Chain/Tiles, the wizard s chain stages, and (via BL-248) the corp roll-ups. TWO CALLS TAKEN WITH BEN, asked with measurements: (a) the Selection band rests EXPANDED-IN-PLACE - its fixed 260px rect cannot shrink, so a folded one-liner would spend ~220px on emptiness, the objection the superseded design raised against Glance-everywhere and which the binary note never resolved; (b) the wizard folds PER CHAIN STAGE. ONE CALL TAKEN ALONE: the overlay JOINS the Esc ladder, one rung below the subject drills - Decision 10 kept depth off it, but reasoned about an in-place stepper, and a full-screen mode with no keyboard exit is a defect. The History Chain s per-stage CollapsingHeader was retired - it was this surface s own private idiom, the fourth one the item exists to kill. 10 goldens blessed and passing.

BL-215.design:
## BL-215 — Render-precision audit: a saved overflow check, not a sweep

**Class:** correctness, not polish. `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` § Container vocabulary (BL-141) already
bans silent truncation of a load-bearing figure. The instances in the wild are that ban being
broken. This item supplies the missing half: **enforcement**.

The one-line statement of intent: *a clipped string should fail a build, not an eyeball.*

---

### 1. The display contract

**The smallest supported display is 1280 x 720 at UI scale 1.0x.**

It is already the contract from two independent directions — the fixed verify/golden capture size
(`verify_w` / `verify_h`, `src/core/app.cpp:71-72`) and the smallest options-menu preset
(`app.cpp:2809`) — but it is asserted in no prose and enforced in no code. Today the only floor is
`std::max(640, …)` on the persisted settings (`app.cpp:2929-2931`), and at 640 wide the shell is
structurally broken: `shell_column_width` returns its 380 floor, `mm_w` returns its 336 floor, and
`380 + 336 + 8 > 640`, so the Selection band's width clamps to zero via `std::max(0.0f, …)`
(`app.cpp:2647`) and the header strip returns early (`header_panel.cpp:54`). It fails soft, silently,
below a width nothing declares unsupported.

The contract becomes real in three places:

1. **`SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize(m_window, 1280 * s, 720 * s)`**, where `s` is the active UI-scale
   factor (1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5). Called on window creation and re-applied from `app::apply_ui_scale()`.
   The floor scales with the font because BL-063 grew the font via atlas reload and never called
   `ImGuiStyle::ScaleAllSizes` — every hard-coded px constant (`margin` 8, `mm_w` floor 336,
   `shell_column_width`'s 380/460 clamp, `selection_band_height` 340, the two 92s, `nav_pane_width`
   56) stays at 1.0x while text grows. At 1.5x the same layout honestly needs 1920 x 1080; the
   min-size call says so instead of letting the player discover it by clipping.
2. **The persisted-settings floor** moves from 640 x 480 to 1280 x 720.
3. **`docs/development/DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md` § Display environment** states it, and the three
   stale figures the recon found are corrected in the same edit (see task 3).

The automated check runs at **1280 x 720 @ 1.0x only**. The higher scale steps are honoured by the
min-size call, not by a second capture pass — a scale-step sweep is deliberately out of scope here.

---

### 2. The primary mechanism — an instrumented overflow ledger

Not a capture sweep. The capture sweep already exists and already fails: the committed 1280 x 720
goldens `scripts/verify/golden/history_chain_round0.png` and `history_chain_round2.png` contain,
between them, a threshold caption clipped to `"ay greenhouse"`, a caption printed over a bar, two
chart titles cut mid-word, a clipped round question, and a legend row whose numeric value is missing
outright — and every one of them was blessed. Under the standing "goldens are disposable" practice
that is by design. A verdict a human reads off a PNG decays into the eyeball pass this item was
filed to replace.

**`src/ui/text_fit.{hpp,cpp}` (namespace `ui`) owns every measured text draw and records the ones
that did not fit.**

```cpp
/// Which of LAYOUT.md's containers a text draw belongs to. Recorded with every
/// overflow so a report names the container whose policy was broken.
enum class text_box : std::uint8_t {
    foldout_column = 1,  ///< 1 — wrap
    canvas_legend,       ///< 2 — guaranteed-fit, box grows
    selection,           ///< 3 — wrap
    header_strip,        ///< 4 — guaranteed-fit, elide-with-tooltip (also the identity tile)
    time_panel,          ///< 5 — guaranteed-fit, authored to fit
    hover_card,          ///< 6 — wrap at max width
    lens_bar,            ///< 7 — icon-only / guaranteed-fit
    nav_rail,            ///< 8 — icon-only, tooltips wrap
    table_cell,          ///< 9 — guaranteed-fit (clip + tooltip) or wrap
    chart_plot,          ///< 10 — guaranteed-fit, reflowing (BL-215)
};

enum class overflow_severity : std::uint8_t {
    elided,      ///< Fitted by eliding, full string one hover away. Sanctioned (4, 9). WARN.
    clipped,     ///< Did not fit and no recovery path existed. FAIL.
    unfittable,  ///< A wrapping box met a single token wider than the box. FAIL.
};

enum class text_align : std::uint8_t { left, right, centre };
```

Behaviour is fixed **per policy**, and the policies are LAYOUT.md's, not new ones:

| Entry point | Policy | Cannot-fit behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `fit_text` | guaranteed-fit | Elide to the widest prefix + `…`; **always** attach the full string via `SetItemTooltip`. If even `…` does not fit, draw nothing, still emit a zero-width `Dummy`, still attach the tooltip, record `clipped`. |
| `wrap_text` | wrap | Wrap; **never** elide (LAYOUT.md § "wrap vs guaranteed-fit is a binary choice per container"). An unbreakable token wider than `max_w` records `unfittable`. |
| `add_fit_text` | guaranteed-fit, draw-list | Elide and record. There is no ImGui item to hang a tooltip on, so a `clipped` record here is a hard signal that the **container** must reflow — that is the fix, not a per-call hack. |

The helper **never** shortens the source string, **never** shrinks the font, and **never** clips
without leaving a record.

Recording is on in Debug builds and unconditionally under `--verify`; off in Release interactive
(the branch guards the `std::string` construction, so the cost when off is one bool test).
Records dedupe on `(site, text)` so a sixty-frame run does not flood the report; the stored record
keeps the first frame label and the worst severity seen.

**How it fails a build.** `app::run_verify` already owns an assertion primitive that bumps
`m_verify_failures` and returns non-zero (`app.cpp:1112-1117`, `:1724-1729`). Two new bindings hang
off it:

- `verify.clipping()` → the running count of `clipped` + `unfittable` records.
- `verify.expect_no_clipping(label)` → logs every FAIL record (container, site, text, needed px,
  available px, frame), adds them to `m_verify_failures`, writes `screenshots/text_overflow.txt`,
  and returns the count.

`app::capture_frame` calls `ui::set_overflow_frame(name)` before rendering, so every record names
the capture it happened in.

**The saved check** is `scripts/verify/text_overflow_floor.lua`, run at 1280 x 720: it walks every
fold-out ledger and every sub-view (`verify.show_panel` + `verify.panel_view`), all three wizard
rounds (`verify.generation_stage`), every lens (`verify.set_overlay`), each Selection-band kind
(`verify.select_tile` / `select_building` / `go_to`), the header strip, the comms panel and the
build ledger — then calls `verify.expect_no_clipping("floor")` once at the end. It captures PNGs
incidentally; the PNGs are **never** the pass criterion.

**Coverage.** The ledger only sees sites that opted in. The complement is one greppable step,
documented in the skill: `rg -n "AddText\(" src/ui src/core` must return only hits inside
`text_fit.cpp`, `icons.cpp`, or lines carrying a trailing `// fit-exempt: <reason>` comment.

---

### 3. The shared helper's API

`src/ui/text_fit.hpp`, namespace `ui`. This is the **one** measured fit-or-wrap utility; every site
uses it, and the 46 inline `CalcTextSize` re-derivations across `src/ui` collapse into it.

```cpp
/// Draw @p text as an ImGui item, elided to @p max_w with a tooltip carrying the
/// full string when it did not fit. Guaranteed-fit containers (2, 4, 5, 7, 9-numeric, 10).
/// @param site Stable literal key naming the draw site, e.g. "header.balance". Reported.
/// @return true when the text was elided.
bool fit_text(text_box box, const char* site, const char* text, float max_w,
              bool disabled = false);

/// Draw @p text wrapped to @p max_w as an ImGui item. Wrapping containers (1, 3, 6, 8, 9-desc).
/// Records `unfittable` when a single unbreakable token exceeds @p max_w — the only
/// way a wrapping box can still clip. Never elides.
void wrap_text(text_box box, const char* site, const char* text, float max_w);

/// Draw-list variant for hand-drawn surfaces with no ImGui item (charts.cpp, the
/// canvas legend boxes). Elides to @p max_w.
/// @param align left = starts at pos.x; right = ENDS at pos.x; centre = centred on pos.x.
/// @return the width actually drawn.
float add_fit_text(ImDrawList* dl, text_box box, const char* site,
                   ImVec2 pos, float max_w, ImU32 col, const char* text,
                   text_align align = text_align::left);

/// The width @p text needs at the current font. Containers that SIZE themselves to
/// their text (2, 5, 7) measure through this rather than CalcTextSize direct, so the
/// measurement and the report cannot disagree.
float fit_width(const char* text);

/// The pure string operation, for hand-drawn hosts that need the fitted string
/// before they know where to put it. Records nothing.
std::string fitted(const char* text, float max_w);
```

Recorder surface:

```cpp
struct text_overflow {
    text_box          box       = text_box::foldout_column;
    const char*       site      = "";
    std::string       text;
    std::string       frame;     ///< Capture name current when it was recorded.
    float             needed    = 0.0f;
    float             available = 0.0f;
    overflow_severity sev       = overflow_severity::elided;
};

void        set_overflow_recording(bool on);
bool        overflow_recording();
void        set_overflow_frame(const std::string& label);
const std::vector<text_overflow>& overflows();
void        clear_overflows();
std::size_t overflow_failures();                     ///< clipped + unfittable
std::size_t write_overflow_report(const char* path); ///< returns the failure count
```

`fit_ellipsis` / `text_ellipsized` in the anonymous namespace of `src/ui/profile_panel.cpp:12-43`
are the existing, correct, unreachable implementation of exactly this. They are **deleted** and
their call sites routed through `fit_text` — that is the first adoption and it proves the API.

---

### 4. LAYOUT.md — the tenth container, admitted deliberately

A hand-drawn chart claims **neither** LAYOUT.md policy: `charts.cpp` measures only to *position*
text (right-align the tick gutter, centre the year labels), never to decide whether the text fits.
That is how it became a tenth container by accident. Naming it is more honest than pretending it is
container 1.

Row 10 is added to the container table:

| # | Container | Sizing | Text policy | Overflow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | **Hand-drawn chart plot** (draw-list, `charts.cpp`) | Host-supplied screen-space box, measured before it is reserved | Guaranteed-fit, **reflowing** — labels measured, the plot's own geometry yields to them | Legend reflows below the plot, then elide-with-record; never silent truncation of a plotted value |

Two further amendments in the same section:

- Container 4's row is widened to name **both** the balance strip (`header_panel.cpp`) and the
  identity tile (`profile_panel.cpp`) — both are fixed-height chrome strips with identical policy,
  and the identity tile was previously covered by no row at all.
- A new closing note: *"Amending this set is a deliberate act, recorded here. Inventing a tenth
  ad hoc is what BL-215 was filed to clean up. Every text draw names its container through
  `ui::text_fit`; a draw that names none is caught by the coverage grep in `verifier-visual`."*

---

### 5. charts.cpp — measure before you reserve

The load-bearing defect is structural, not cosmetic: `chart_row_height(float chart_h)`
(`charts.cpp:51-56`) commits the box **height** at `generation_charts.cpp:198`, while the width
`cw` is not read until `:205`. No width-derived decision was reachable, so no narrow-host behaviour
could exist. The fix is a measure-first API fed by a width the caller already has — `col_w`,
computed at `generation_charts.cpp:182-186` for the one-column/two-column decision.

```cpp
enum class legend_place : std::uint8_t { beside, below, none };

/// Width the swatch legend needs: 16 (swatch + gap) + the widest "label value" + 8.
/// Replaces the file-local `constexpr float legend_w = 190.0f`, which was a guess
/// unreconciled with the `lx` the legend actually draws at.
float legend_width(const bar* bars, std::size_t count, const char* fmt);

/// Everything a chart row's geometry needs, answered from the box width the host
/// already knows — so the reserve and the draw cannot disagree.
struct chart_metrics {
    float        chart_h     = 0.0f;
    int          title_lines = 1;                    ///< 1 or 2; beyond 2 the title elides.
    int          legend_rows = 0;                    ///< 0 when the legend sits beside.
    legend_place place       = legend_place::beside;
};
chart_metrics measure_chart(float box_w, const char* title,
                            const bar* bars, std::size_t count,
                            const char* fmt, float chart_h);

float chart_row_height(const chart_metrics& m);
float chart_row_height(float chart_h);   ///< kept VERBATIM — the tile-selection golden depends on it.
```

`draw_bars` gains a trailing `legend_place place = legend_place::beside`. **The mode is a caller
opt-in, never a width test inside the function**: `charts.hpp:57` promises the two-bar,
`bar_cap = 34.0f` tile-selection graphs are pixel-identical, and their host width at 1280 is ~238 px
— narrower than the fold-out chart — so any naive `cw < 300` test would move that golden.

Four further corrections inside the file, all by policy:

- **Legend reserve.** `place == below` sets the reserve to 0 at `charts.cpp:94`, so the column band
  goes from its 60 px floor to the full plot width and the History ledger's squeezed bars unsqueeze.
  Below-legend entries flow left-to-right under `mx.y`, wrapping by measurement.
- **Tick gutter.** `gutter = 40.0f` is fixed and a 5-digit ceiling overruns left of `mn.x`. Labels
  format through the existing `fmt::abbreviate` (`src/ui/format.hpp:33`) instead of `%g`, and the
  plot uses a measured `g = std::max(gutter, fit_width(top_label) + 6.0f)`. `charts::gutter` stays
  as the constant hosts indent titles by. The top tick's `ty - ts.y * 0.5f` is clamped into the box
  so it stops printing into the title row.
- **Threshold caption.** `threshold_line` takes the resolved legend reserve so caption and band
  cannot disagree by construction, and degrades in a stated ladder: right-aligned within the band →
  left-aligned at `plot_x0` just *below* the line → `add_fit_text` at the plot width.
- **Time-series axes.** The right-hand tick at `px1 + 5` needs 45 px in a 40 px gutter; both gutters
  become measured the same way, and both axes' labels route through `add_fit_text`.

Chart **titles wrap** to at most two lines (counted by `measure_chart`, drawn under
`PushTextWrapPos`), then elide with a tooltip. A title is prose, not a load-bearing figure —
shortening the string is the fix this item exists to forbid, and nine of the History ledger's titles
are over the 32-character budget precisely because someone will edit them again.

---

### 6. The remaining sites

| Site | Container | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `profile_panel.cpp:12-43` | 4 | Delete the private `fit_ellipsis` / `text_ellipsized`; route through `fit_text(text_box::header_strip, …)`. |
| `header_panel.cpp:97-114` | 4 | Keep the existing drop ladder (debt flag, then the 96 px sparkline) — it is correct and it runs **before** any elision. The three numbers then draw through `fit_text`. |
| `tile_inspector.cpp:175` | 1 | `cr.question` is a bare `TextDisabled` in a wrapping container → `wrap_text(text_box::foldout_column, …)`. |
| `chat_panel.cpp:77-99` | 1 | The channel tab strip is a straight `SameLine` chain that clips silently. Measure each `SmallButton` and break to a new line rather than clipping. |
| `selection_panel.cpp:695` | 3 | Route through `fit_width`. |
| `body_surface_canvas.cpp:419-422, 459-465` | 2 | Already the measure-then-size pattern LAYOUT.md cites as precedent — route through `fit_width` / `add_fit_text` so the boxes participate in the report rather than being trusted. |

---

### 7. Relationship to BL-063 and BL-214

**BL-063 (accessibility / legibility baseline) — keep separate, no merge.** It is `complete`
(landed 287d8e0) and cannot absorb open work; its remit is contrast and scale, BL-215's is geometry
and truncation. The one real coupling — the font grows, the px constants do not — is owned here as
the scale-proportional display floor (§1). When `docs/ui/ACCESSIBILITY.md` is eventually authored it
**cites** LAYOUT.md's container vocabulary as the geometry half rather than restating it. BL-063's
open follow-up (wiring `palette::text_secondary` into the ~90 `TextDisabled` sites) touches
overlapping files and should be sequenced **after** BL-215, so it edits sites already routed through
`ui::text_fit`.

**BL-214 (drill-through idiom)** shares `charts.cpp`, `generation_charts.cpp` and `LAYOUT.md`.
BL-215 goes first: BL-214's point 5 ("at GLANCE the explainers should probably not render at all
rather than be truncated") is a decision about *what to show*, and it is much easier to make once
truncation is a measurable, failing condition rather than a judgement call.

---

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

1. **The smallest supported display is 1280 x 720 @ 1.0x, and it is enforced** via
   `SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize` scaled by the UI-scale factor, plus a persisted-settings floor moved
   from 640 x 480. It was already the contract in two places and stated in none.
2. **The primary check is an instrumented overflow ledger, not a capture sweep.** A capture sweep
   already exists and already passed six real clipping defects into committed goldens; a ledger
   produces an integer that fails a build. The sweep survives only as the script's incidental output.
3. **The severity ladder is three-way** — `elided` (sanctioned, WARN), `clipped` (FAIL),
   `unfittable` (FAIL) — so the check enforces LAYOUT.md's actual policy rather than crying wolf on
   the elide-with-tooltip degradation LAYOUT.md explicitly permits.
4. **One shared helper, `src/ui/text_fit.{hpp,cpp}`**, with four entry points; `profile_panel.cpp`'s
   private `fit_ellipsis` / `text_ellipsized` are deleted into it.
5. **When text cannot fit even wrapped**: never shorten the string, never shrink the font, never
   clip without a record. Guaranteed-fit always leaves a tooltip; wrap never elides; the draw-list
   variant records and the container must reflow.
6. **A tenth container is admitted deliberately** — hand-drawn chart plot, guaranteed-fit and
   reflowing — rather than pretending `charts.cpp` obeys container 1.
7. **Chart titles wrap (max two lines, then elide-with-tooltip); the legend reflows below the plot.**
   The narrow-host mode is a **caller opt-in**, not an internal width test, because a width test
   would move the tile-selection golden `charts.hpp:57` promises is pixel-identical.
8. **`legend_w = 190.0f` becomes measured**, and the tick gutters become measured, because both
   fixed guesses are the direct cause of confirmed clipping in the committed goldens.
9. **BL-063 stays separate** (it is complete; orthogonal remit), with one stated coupling and a
   sequencing note for its `text_secondary` follow-up.
10. **The check extends `verifier-visual`** rather than becoming a new skill, plus a greppable
    coverage step for sites that never opted in. Skill edits need permission; if denied, run the
    script ad hoc and note it in the requirement.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben delegated these calls for the ultracode session and was unavailable; each is recorded here so it can be reviewed or overturned.

**Q. What is the smallest supported display — the stated contract?**

- **Decision:** 1280 x 720 at UI scale 1.0x, and it is ENFORCED, not merely stated. `SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize` is called with `1280 * s, 720 * s` where `s` is the active UI-scale factor (1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5), re-applied from `app::apply_ui_scale()`. The persisted-settings floor in `app.cpp:2929-2931` moves from 640x480 to 1280x720. The contract is checked at 1280x720 @ 1.0x only; the higher scale steps are honoured by the min-size call, not by a second capture pass.
- **Why:** 1280x720 is already the de-facto contract from two independent directions — it is the fixed verify/golden capture size (`verify_w`/`verify_h`, app.cpp:71-72) and the smallest options-menu preset (app.cpp:2809) — but it is asserted nowhere and enforced nowhere. The recon shows the shell is structurally broken below ~1024 wide (at 640 the Selection band's width clamps to 0 and the header returns early), so the existing 640x480 floor is a lie that fails soft instead of failing loudly. Making the floor a real `SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize` turns 'the width it was authored against' into a width the OS will not let you go below. Scaling the floor with the font is the honest consequence of BL-063 having grown the font without calling `ScaleAllSizes` — at 1.5x the same layout genuinely needs 1920x1080, so the min-size call states that rather than letting the user discover it by clipping.

**Q. Can clipping be CHECKED rather than eyeballed? Pick ONE primary mechanism and specify it.**

- **Decision:** Yes. The primary mechanism is an INSTRUMENTED OVERFLOW LEDGER, not a capture sweep. A new `src/ui/text_fit.{hpp,cpp}` module owns every measured text draw; each call names its LAYOUT.md container and a stable site key, and when the text does not fit its box the module records a `ui::text_overflow` classified as `elided` (fitted with a tooltip — sanctioned for containers 4 and 9, WARN only), `clipped` (did not fit with no recovery path — FAIL) or `unfittable` (a single unbreakable token wider than a wrapping box — FAIL). Recording is on in Debug builds and unconditionally under `--verify`, off in Release interactive. Two new Lua bindings in `app::run_verify` — `verify.clipping()` and `verify.expect_no_clipping(label)` — expose the ledger; `expect_no_clipping` adds each FAIL record to the existing `m_verify_failures` counter, so the harness exits non-zero exactly the way a golden miss does, and writes `screenshots/text_overflow.txt`. One new saved script, `scripts/verify/text_overflow_floor.lua`, walks the whole shell at 1280x720 and asserts zero. A capture sweep is retained only as the script's incidental PNG output, never as the pass criterion.
- **Why:** The item asks which is more valuable and the answer is not close. The recon proves the capture sweep already exists and already fails: the committed goldens `history_chain_round0.png` and `history_chain_round2.png` contain, in one frame each, a clipped threshold caption, a caption over a bar, two clipped chart titles, a clipped round question, and a legend row whose numeric value is missing entirely — and every one of them was blessed. A check whose verdict is a human looking at a PNG decays into the same eyeball pass BL-215 was filed to replace, and 'goldens are disposable' (standing practice) means the images get re-blessed without review by design. A ledger produces an integer that fails a build. It also enforces the thing LAYOUT.md actually bans — a POLICY violation — rather than a pixel appearance: the call site must name its container, so a new surface cannot silently invent a tenth policy. Rejected alternatives: a debug-build assert at every text-draw site (an assert cannot distinguish sanctioned elide-with-tooltip from banned silent truncation, so it would either fire constantly or be disabled); post-hoc analysis of `ImDrawData` (ImGui culls fully-clipped glyphs at build time, so the evidence is gone before we could read it, and it could never name the container whose policy was broken).

**Q. What is the shared helper's API — name, exact signature, location, and behaviour when text cannot fit even wrapped?**

- **Decision:** Module `src/ui/text_fit.{hpp,cpp}`, namespace `ui`. Four draw entry points — `bool fit_text(text_box, const char* site, const char* text, float max_w, bool disabled = false)` (ImGui item, elide policy, tooltip when elided); `void wrap_text(text_box, const char* site, const char* text, float max_w)` (wrap policy); `float add_fit_text(ImDrawList*, text_box, const char* site, ImVec2 pos, float max_w, ImU32 col, const char* text, text_align align = text_align::left)` (draw-list hosts with no ImGui item); `float fit_width(const char* text)` (measure-only, for containers that size themselves to their text). Plus `std::string fitted(const char* text, float max_w)` for hand-drawn hosts that need the string before positioning. Cannot-fit behaviour, by policy: `fit_text` elides to the widest prefix + ellipsis and always attaches the full string as `SetItemTooltip`; if even the ellipsis does not fit it draws nothing, still emits a zero-width `Dummy`, still attaches the tooltip, and records `clipped`. `wrap_text` wraps and never elides (mixing the two policies inside one container is banned by LAYOUT.md); an unbreakable token wider than `max_w` records `unfittable`. `add_fit_text` elides and records; it has no tooltip to offer, so a `clipped` record there is a hard signal that the CONTAINER must reflow. The helper never shortens the source string, never shrinks the font, and never clips without a record.
- **Why:** Exactly one implementation of this pattern exists today — `fit_ellipsis` / `text_ellipsized` in an anonymous namespace in `profile_panel.cpp:12-43`, i.e. the right code in the wrong scope — while 46 raw `CalcTextSize` sites re-derive it inline. One module, one measurement, one recorder is the legible answer; every site measuring for itself is how the report and the reality drift apart. The `site` string literal is what makes the report actionable ('charts.legend' beats 'a string somewhere clipped'), and the `text_box` parameter is what makes the check an enforcement of LAYOUT.md rather than a generic width warning. The three-way cannot-fit ladder is chosen so that the value is never silently lost (there is always a tooltip or a record), while the sanctioned degradations LAYOUT.md already permits stay non-failing — otherwise the check would cry wolf on the header strip's own documented behaviour and be turned off.

**Q. charts.cpp: how is the narrow-host mode specified, and is a hand-drawn chart a tenth container?**

- **Decision:** Admit the tenth container, deliberately: LAYOUT.md gains row 10, 'Hand-drawn chart plot (draw-list, `charts.cpp`)' — sizing: host-supplied screen-space box; text policy: guaranteed-fit, REFLOWING; overflow: reflow the legend below the plot, then elide-with-record. The implementation is a measure-first API: `charts::legend_width(const bar*, count, fmt)` replaces the file-local `constexpr float legend_w = 190.0f`; a new `struct chart_metrics { float chart_h; int title_lines; int legend_rows; }` and `chart_metrics measure_chart(float box_w, const char* title, const bar* bars, std::size_t count, const char* fmt, float chart_h)` answer 'how tall, how many title lines, legend beside or below' from a width the caller already knows; `chart_row_height(const chart_metrics&)` is the new overload, with `chart_row_height(float)` kept verbatim so the goldened tile-selection graphs are untouched. `draw_bars` gains a trailing `legend_place place = legend_place::beside` parameter — the mode is a CALLER opt-in, never a raw width test inside the function. The tick gutter becomes measured (`max(gutter, fit_width(top_label) + 6)`) with labels formatted through the existing `fmt::abbreviate` instead of `%g`, and the top tick's y is clamped into the box. `threshold_line` takes the resolved legend reserve so caption and band cannot disagree, and degrades right-aligned-in-band -> left-aligned-below-the-line -> `add_fit_text`. Chart TITLES wrap to at most two lines (counted by `measure_chart`, drawn under `PushTextWrapPos`), then elide with a tooltip.
- **Why:** charts.cpp claims neither of LAYOUT.md's two policies — it measures only to POSITION text (right-align, centre), never to decide whether the text fits — which is precisely how it became a tenth container by accident. Naming it is more honest than pretending it is container 1: it genuinely has a distinct sizing rule (a screen-space box handed down by a host, drawn to a draw list with no ImGui items), and LAYOUT.md's 'do not invent a tenth' is a rule against ad-hoc invention, not against amending the closed set on the record. The load-bearing bug is structural, not cosmetic: `chart_row_height(chart_h)` commits the box HEIGHT before `cw` is read at generation_charts.cpp:205, so no width-derived decision was reachable; `measure_chart` fed by the already-computed `col_w` (generation_charts.cpp:182-186) closes that hole and makes the reserve and the draw provably agree. The caller opt-in is required by the recon's warning that a naive `cw < 300` test also fires on the tile-selection graphs (cw ~238) and would move a golden that charts.hpp:57 promises is pixel-identical. Titles wrap rather than elide because a title is prose, not a load-bearing figure — the item's rule 3 says fix by policy, and wrapping is the policy that keeps the whole string.

**Q. Reconcile with BL-063 (accessibility / legibility baseline) — merge or keep separate?**

- **Decision:** Keep separate. No merge. BL-063 is `complete` (landed 287d8e0) and cannot absorb open work; its remit is CONTRAST and SCALE, BL-215's is GEOMETRY and TRUNCATION. They touch at exactly one seam, and BL-215 owns it explicitly: BL-063 grew the font via atlas reload without ever calling `ImGuiStyle::ScaleAllSizes`, so every hard-coded px constant stays at 1.0x while text grows — that is why the display floor is stated PER SCALE STEP here and encoded in the scale-proportional `SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize`. Cross-reference only: `docs/ui/ACCESSIBILITY.md` (BL-063's authority_doc, not yet authored) shall cite LAYOUT.md's container vocabulary as the geometry half rather than restate it. BL-063's own open follow-up — wiring `palette::text_secondary` into the ~90 `TextDisabled` sites — is a separate sweep over overlapping files; sequence it AFTER BL-215 so it edits sites that have already been routed through `ui::text_fit`.
- **Why:** Merging a design-owed item into a complete one destroys the closed item's audit trail and gives the merged item two authority docs (ACCESSIBILITY.md and LAYOUT.md) with no rule for which wins. The remits are genuinely orthogonal: a perfectly legible string at 7:1 contrast that is cut off mid-word fails BL-215 and passes BL-063, and vice versa. What DOES need reconciling is the one real coupling — scale versus fixed px — and that is a single stated rule, not a merged backlog item. Sequencing the `text_secondary` sweep second is a courtesy that avoids two passes rewriting the same ~90 call sites in opposite orders.

**Q. Where does the saved check live — a new skill, or an extension of an existing one?**

- **Decision:** Extend `verifier-visual`. The check runs through the existing `ProjectIo --verify` harness, so it is a new script (`scripts/verify/text_overflow_floor.lua`) plus a named section in `.claude/skills/verifier-visual/SKILL.md` — no new skill. The SKILL.md section states that the harness now writes `screenshots/text_overflow.txt` and exits non-zero on any `clipped`/`unfittable` record, and adds one greppable COVERAGE step: `rg -n "AddText\(" src/ui src/core` must return only hits inside `text_fit.cpp`, `icons.cpp`, or lines carrying a trailing `// fit-exempt: <reason>` comment. Per CLAUDE.md, modifying a skill needs the user's permission: attempt the SKILL.md edit; if denied, run the script as a one-off this session and record in the requirement's Notes that the method was run ad hoc.
- **Why:** A second skill wrapping the same binary with the same invocation would be duplication, and the discovery problem the 'tool creation is skill creation' rule solves is already solved by `verifier-visual` — the script is auto-discovered from `scripts/verify/`. The coverage grep is the necessary complement to the ledger: the ledger only sees sites that opted in, so a brand-new surface that draws raw `AddText` is invisible to it. Keeping the grep as a documented step rather than a build-breaking lint is proportionate — it is a one-line command with an explicit exemption idiom, and the exemption comment is itself the reviewable artifact.
BL-215.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (build-heavy v0.1.1 batch, worktree agent). ui::text_fit module (10-container enum, elided/clipped/unfittable ledger, (site,text) dedupe); profile_panel's private fit_ellipsis deleted into it; SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize(1280*s,720*s) + persisted floor 1280x720 + DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment; charts measure-first rework (legend_width, chart_metrics/measure_chart, legend_place caller opt-in, measured gutters, chart_row_height(float) verbatim); § 6 sites adopted; verify.clipping()/expect_no_clipping + scripts/verify/text_overflow_floor.lua (PASS on the integrated tree, 0 clipped/unfittable — one real overflow found and fixed: beside-mode legends under-reserved by 12px inter-column offset); LAYOUT.md row 10 + container 4 widened; coverage grep clean; verifier-visual SKILL.md § Text-overflow floor check (Ben approved 2026-08-09). Open riders: NR-107 (tick abbreviate >=1000 only), NR-108 (tile-selection golden drift, re-bless on Windows). requirements.json § text-wrap-render-audit R1-R6 complete.

BL-216.design:
## BL-216 — Shell re-plan: comms to the bottom band, pinned items to the freed centre-right

**Status: designed, 2026-07-30.** Ben settled the two blocking questions (comms gets its own rect
left of the Selection band; pinned items are built for real). Everything below is settled on his
behalf and is authoritative for implementation. The item's original sequencing note (behind
BL-215/BL-214) is **overridden** — Ben authorised this now.

---

### 1. The shape

The bottom of the screen becomes **one strip with two tiles**, sandwiched as before between the
full-height shell column and the full-height right chrome column:

```
┌──────────┬─────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
│ Profile  │     │           Header             │  Time panel  │
├──────────┤     ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Nav rail │Fold-│                              │              │
│ (icons)  │out  │       Primary canvas         │ PINNED ITEMS │
│ ▢ ▢ ▦ …  │col  │                              │ (watch list) │
│          │(full│                              ├──────────────┤
│          │hght)├────────┬─────────────────────┤   Minimap    │
│          │     │ COMMS  │  SELECTION BAND     │  [lens bar]  │
└──────────┴─────┴────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────┘
```

The **fold-out ledger column is untouched** — it still runs `profile_panel_height → disp.y`, so the
BL-117 one-question-per-view splits keep the vertical budget they were sized against. Comms starts
at `x = shell_column_width(disp.x)`, so column and dock are horizontally disjoint; nothing occludes
anything.

---

### 2. Rect algebra — one owner

Recon hazard #1 is that `disp.x - margin - mm_w` is re-derived **five times** in `app.cpp`
(`:2291`, `:2414`, `:2509`, `:2585`, `:2645`) with no owning function. Adding a fourth region on top
of that guarantees drift. So the foundation of this item is a new module.

**`src/ui/shell_metrics.{hpp,cpp}`** — the single home of the shell's rect algebra. It *consumes*
`shell_column_width` / `foldout_column_rect` (which stay in `foldout_column.hpp`) and does not
duplicate them.

```cpp
namespace ui {

struct shell_rect { float x, y, w, h; };

inline constexpr float shell_margin             = 8.0f;   // the screen gutter app.cpp uses
inline constexpr float comms_rail_width         = nav_pane_width;  // 56 — the shell's collapsed-strip idiom
inline constexpr float comms_dock_min_width     = 300.0f;
inline constexpr float comms_dock_max_width     = 440.0f;
inline constexpr float comms_dock_band_reserve  = 560.0f; // band width the dock must leave behind to dock

enum class comms_dock_mode { docked, railed };

float       right_chrome_width(ImVec2 disp);   // max(336, 0.28 * min(disp.x, disp.y))  == mm_w
float       right_chrome_left (ImVec2 disp);   // disp.x - shell_margin - right_chrome_width(disp)
shell_rect  minimap_rect      (ImVec2 disp);
float       bottom_band_budget(ImVec2 disp);   // max(0, right_chrome_left - shell_column_width)

comms_dock_mode comms_dock_mode_for(ImVec2 disp);
shell_rect  comms_dock_rect     (ImVec2 disp);          // docked: full panel; railed: 56px strip
shell_rect  comms_peek_rect     (ImVec2 disp);          // railed-mode overlay, over the band
shell_rect  selection_band_rect (ImVec2 disp);
shell_rect  pinned_panel_rect   (ImVec2 disp, float time_h);

} // namespace ui
```

**Comms dock width:**

```
budget = bottom_band_budget(disp)
wanted = clamp(round(0.32f * budget), comms_dock_min_width, comms_dock_max_width)
dock_w = (wanted <= budget - comms_dock_band_reserve) ? wanted
       : (budget >= comms_rail_width ? comms_rail_width : 0.0f)
```

All widths are rounded to whole pixels, exactly as `shell_column_width` already does, so every
region edge lands on a pixel boundary.

**Selection band:** `x = shell_column_width(disp.x) + dock_w`, `w = max(0, budget - dock_w)`,
`y = disp.y - selection_band_height`, `h = selection_band_height` (340, **unchanged**).
There is **no gap** between the dock and the band — the band is already flush against the shell
column and the right chrome, and introducing the shell's only gutter here would read as a mistake.

**Resolved, at every supported size:**

| Display | `mm_w` | `right` | `W` | budget | mode | dock_w | band.w | (band today) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 × 720  | 336   | 936  | 380 | 556  | **railed** | 56  | **500**  | 556 |
| 1600 × 900  | 336   | 1256 | 380 | 876  | docked | 300 | 576  | 876 |
| 1720 × 1080 | 336   | 1376 | 380 | 996  | docked | 319 | 677  | 996 |
| 1920 × 1080 | 336   | 1576 | 384 | 1192 | docked | 381 | 811  | 1192 |
| 2560 × 1440 | 403.2 | 2149 | 460 | 1689 | docked | 440 | 1249 | 1689 |

The dock threshold falls at **≈1584 px display width** — the 1600×900 preset and up dock; 1280×720
rails. At the 640×480 settings floor `budget` clamps to 0, `dock_w` to 0 and `band.w` to 0: the same
fail-soft the band already has, no new failure mode.

---

### 3. The smallest supported display — measured, not clamped

**1280 × 720 has 556 px for the whole bottom band** (1280 − 380 shell column − 344 right chrome).
There is no honest width assignment that seats a readable comms panel *and* the BL-213 tile
three-column layout in 556 px. Rather than clamp comms to a sliver or pretend, the layout states
the threshold and degrades into an idiom the shell already owns:

- **Railed mode.** The dock renders as a **56 px full-band-height rail** at `x = W` — the same width
  as `nav_pane_width`, so it reads as a second vertical rail rhyming with the nav rail across the
  bottom-left corner. It carries the `icons::pin`-family comms glyph, an **unread badge**, and the
  newest speaker's identity swatch. Container policy: **container 8** (icon-only, tooltip wraps).
- **Peek.** Clicking the rail toggles `ui_state::comms_peek`, drawing the full comms panel at
  `comms_peek_rect` — the band's rect, `x = band.x`, `w = min(comms_dock_max_width, band.w)` —
  **after** the band in draw order, so it wins z-order. Re-clicking the rail closes it (the standing
  toggle rule: its active state is visible, so re-click undoes). Esc also closes it.
- **Cost, stated:** at 1280 the band goes 556 → 500 px (≈10%). The tile layout's quarters go
  139 → 125 and its centre 262 → 234. Tight, and already tight; BL-215 is the item that makes narrow
  hosts render correctly, and it inherits this width as its target.

**The docked/railed choice is purely derived from `disp`.** There is no player collapse toggle:
the band's rect stays a pure function of display size, with no hidden state to get stuck in.
`comms_peek` is the only comms state, and it is forced `false` every frame in docked mode.

---

### 4. Comms — internal re-layout for the new host

At 1720×1080 comms goes **336 × 698 → 319 × 340**: essentially the same width, half the rows. The
problem is *vertical*, so every change buys rows. All of it stays inside the existing
wrap + vertical-scroll policy — no measured boxes, no new text policy.

1. **Fold the label into the control row.** The standalone `TextDisabled("COMMS")` + `Separator`
   (`chat_panel.cpp:73-74`) goes; `COMMS` becomes a leading dim label on the channel row. *Buys a
   text line + a separator.*
2. **One-line message form.** Replace the two-line stanza (`TextWrapped` day+speaker, then
   `Indent()` + `TextWrapped(body)` + `Unindent()`, `:152-158`) with a **single wrapped paragraph**:
   dim `d%d `, then the speaker in its identity colour, then `": "` — each via `SameLine(0.0f, 0.0f)`
   — then `TextWrapped(body)`. System lines (`from == null_entity`) stay one dim wrapped line.
   *Buys ~40% of rows.*
3. **Channel selector, not a tab chain.** The `SameLine` chain of `SmallButton`s (`:77-99`) has **no
   overflow handling** and clips silently — a real defect the narrower dock would expose. Replace it
   with a single-row `ImGui::BeginCombo` over `chat.channels` plus the `"+"` button on the same line.
   A channel selector is a **cross-cutting selector** and therefore explicitly exempt from the toggle
   rule, so this costs no rule complexity. *Buys unbounded channel count in one fixed row.*
4. **Cap the group popup.** `SetNextWindowSizeConstraints({220,0},{320,260})` and put the per-corp
   checkbox list (`:107-114`) inside `BeginChild("##grp_members", {0.0f, 160.0f})` so it scrolls
   instead of growing unbounded upward from a bottom-anchored popup.
5. **Floor guard.** Keep `if (height <= 0.0f) return;` and add `if (height < 120.0f) return;` — below
   that ImGui clamps the log child's negative height to 4 px and pushes the input row out of the
   window. Defensive only (height is always 340 today).
6. **Unread counters.** `chat_state` gains `int posted_total = 0;` (incremented in `chat_post`) and
   `int seen_total = 0;` (set to `posted_total` on every frame the panel *body* draws, docked or
   peeked). Unread = `max(0, posted_total - seen_total)`, displayed on the rail badge, capped `9+`.
   Counters rather than `messages.size()` because the 300-line ring saturates.
7. **New entry point** in `chat_panel.hpp`:
   `void draw_chat_rail(const world&, const chat_state&, ui_state&, float x, float y, float w, float h);`
   `draw_chat_panel`'s signature is **unchanged** (the 4-float convention); only its doc comment
   changes — `chat_panel.hpp:61-73` currently hard-codes "right shell band … below the time column,
   above the minimap" and "@param x Left edge (aligned with the minimap)".

---

### 5. Pinned items — a real surface

The freed centre-right slot is **exactly** the rect comms vacates:
`{right_chrome_left(disp), shell_margin + time_h + shell_margin, right_chrome_width(disp),
minimap_rect(disp).y - shell_margin - y}` — 336 × ~698 @1720×1080, 336 × ~338 @1280×720.

**The minimap does not move**, and the right column's vertical budget keeps today's two-way elastic
split: time panel (content-derived `time_h`) on top, **pins take the whole residual**, minimap +
lens bar locked bottom-right (`mm_h = 0.75 · mm_w`). The feared three-way split never happens —
comms *leaves* as pins *arrive*. It is a swap, not an addition.

#### What a pin is

A **watch card**: a title row (`draw_selection_icon` kind glyph, entity name, then right-aligned
`[>]` go-to and `[x]` unpin) over the shared **`entity_summary`** stat block for that entity —
`draw_body_summary` / `draw_tile_summary` / `draw_building_summary` / `draw_market_summary` /
`draw_unit_summary` / `draw_nation_summary` / `draw_corporation_summary`. That covers every
`selection_kind` except `none`, so no kind is unpinnable.

**It is deliberately not the Selection band's action content.** Those builders
(`draw_selection_content`, `draw_tile_selection`, `draw_building_selection`, `draw_selection_action`,
`draw_selection_facts`) are entity-*implicit* — every one reads `ui.selected_entity` — and they
mutate singletons: `card_resource_page` is **bound by reference** and paged in place,
`card_stack` is a single drill stack, `show_build_ledger` + `construction.pending_*` are single
per-frame slots. Hosting them twice needs entity threading through five functions plus per-host
keying of three singletons. `entity_summary` is already entity-parameterised, already the sanctioned
second-host path (`draw_hover_card` uses it), already **mandated** by LAYOUT.md § Ledger family
conventions for shared per-entity stat blocks, contains exactly one widget id, writes no `ui_state`
and tolerates stale ids.

**Pins are a watch list, not a second action surface.** Acting on a pin is one click away: clicking
it makes it the selection and the band shows the full action content. In BL-214's terms the pin sits
at the shallow rung and the band at the deep one; BL-214 may re-level it, and this is the pre-
registration for that.

**ID collision:** two market pins would share `BeginTable("market_summary", …)`. Every pin card is
wrapped in `ImGui::PushID(static_cast<int>(entity))` / `PopID()`. That is the whole fix.

#### Rules

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Cap** | `ui::pinned_items_max = 6`. Panel scrolls when cards exceed the height. |
| **Cap reached** | The band's pin button renders **disabled** with tooltip *"Pin list full (6) - unpin one first."* — never a silent drop. |
| **Order** | Append at the end; never reorder. A watch list is learned by position. |
| **Persistence** | **Session-local, not serialised** — matching `chat_state` and every other `ui_state` field. Rides the BL-202/BL-205-slice-2 landing when commands become world state. |
| **Destroyed entity** | Pruned **silently** by `ui::prune_pins(w, ui)` at the top of `draw_pinned_panel` (drops any id where `selection_kind_of(w,id) == none`). SELECTION.md already says "treat a missing id as no selection". |
| **Click a pin** | **Single-click** the card body → `ui.selected_entity = id; ui.selection_hidden_for = null_entity;` (band opens on it). **Double-click** → `focus_on_entity(w, ui, id)`. The `[>]` button does the double-click. This is SELECTION.md's uniform click model, extended — not a new gesture. |
| **Empty state** | Dim wrapped text: *"No pinned items. Use the [pin] button on the Selection band to watch an entity here."* An unexplained empty first-class surface was the Explorer's original sin. |
